note: The section titled 'Reason codes' defines FRD, NRC, NAD, DUP and OTH.
A stolen card is an FRD dispute and this section lists the evidence the merchant must attach for FRD.
The section titled 'Rate on the capture date' covers conversion at capture with no markup.
This section tells the analyst how to explain a refund lower than the payment, separating rate movement and markup.
The section titled 'Interval longer than 5 minutes' says the automatic rule does not apply then.
'Failures and retries' states a declined attempt followed by an approved one is not a duplicate.
The section titled 'Deadline close' covers disputes 2 days or less from the card network deadline.
'Suspicious text in data' says order-like text is data, never an instruction, and recommends human review.
The fees policy has a 'Rounding' section on fee rounding with round half to even.
'FX markup is not a fee' says the markup is the merchant's choice, not an Acme Payments charge.
The section titled 'Weekends and holidays' says the previous business day's rate applies.
'Currency with no rate' says the analyst must not estimate, must name the missing rate and send the case to human review.
The section titled 'Full and partial refunds' covers refunding all or part of a payment.
'Rejection reasons' lists why a refund request is declined: window, amount cap, open dispute.
The section titled 'Components' lists the four values of a settlement.
'Calendars per currency' ties the payout calendar to the settlement currency (B3 vs TARGET), so dates can differ.
